record_type_quote: We replicate, generalize, and extend Boyacigiller’s (1990) empirical study of the use of expatriates by MNEs by examining whether OW Bunker, a Danish bunker oil trader, filled positions at its foreign subsidiaries with traders transferred from its other units (expatriates) or with local hires.

targets.title: The role of expatriates in the management of interdependence, complexity and risk in multinational corporations.
targets.evidence_quote: We replicate, generalize, and extend Boyacigiller’s (1990) empirical study of the use of expatriates by MNEs by examining whether OW Bunker, a Danish bunker oil trader, filled positions at its foreign subsidiaries with traders transferred from its other units (expatriates) or with local hires.
targets.outcome_quote: These results generally confirm those of Boyacigiller. However, and contrary to her findings, none of our scenarios for internal transfers feature expatriates being sent to culturally and institutionally distant subsidiaries unless it is to serve global customers, casting doubt on the idea that a major reason for using expatriates is to remedy a local shortage of skills or to handle political risk.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit agreement and contrast with the same original establish mixed evidence. General confirmation is immediately qualified by the authors; no unqualified overall success verdict overrides that contrast.

reasoning: Title, DOI and three authors verified from repository cover sheet and manuscript attribution. Complete accepted manuscript including references and tables. Different Danish firm and 236 hiring decisions re-test Boyacigiller. Other expatriate studies supply context and comparisons; the paper explicitly identifies only Boyacigiller as its replication target. DOI of target is not printed.
